name: Nordnorsk Kunstmuseum
watch: The regional art museum for Northern Norway, with a strong Sámi programme. It opened a Bodø venue in 2025 and programmes Nordover in Longyearbyen.
records_note: The museum names its 2024 to 2027 board and files accounts in Norway's register, but posts no annual reports and no funder list.

name: Nottingham Contemporary
funding: Arts Council England is principal funder. Headline supporters include Bloomberg Philanthropies and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation (UK Branch); Nottingham City Council, two universities and trusts also give.
watch: Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune counts as fossil-fuel money. In July 2020, 25 current and former staff sent an open letter to its leadership.
records_note: Names supporters by tier with no date and lists ten board members; no annual reports posted, accounts for 2021 to 2025 sit on the register.

name: NTU Centre for Contemporary Art Singapore
funding: Nanyang Technological University research centre; EU-funded SEA AiR residency; public research grants. Budget not found.
watch: Exhibitions and residencies halted Mar 2021 after Economic Development Board funding ended. No donor list is published; research grants name no funders.
records_note: No records of its own; parent NTU posts annual reports 2016 to 2026 with audited accounts; the centre lists its Governing Council.

name: Nubuke Foundation
funding: Private foundation from 2006. Funded through the EU and OACPS ACP-EU Culture programme (AWA consortium with Institut français) and the British Council Digital Collaboration Fund.
watch: Runs the Centre for Clay and Textiles in Wa. The funders page gives no years. No oil, mining or other flagged funder found.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the Funders page names the EU, British Council and Google Arts and Culture, undated, and six board members are listed.

name: Nýló (The Living Art Museum / Nýlistasafnið)
funding: Ministry of Culture and Business Affairs Iceland, City of Reykjavík, member association; artist-run museum foundation.
watch: Founded in 1978 by visual artists as an artist-run museum and archive for experimental and Fluxus art. Based in Marshall House.

name: O—Overgaden Institut for Samtidskunst
funding: Danish Arts Foundation (Statens Kunstfond), City of Copenhagen, private non-profit foundations; registered non-profit.
watch: Founded in 1986 on Christianshavn canal; non-profit institution dedicated to experimental Danish and international artists.

name: Oakville Galleries
funding: Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council, Government of Ontario, Town of Oakville, Mondriaan Fund. Sponsors: Hatch, Taglieri Group, Siemens, Chatsworth Fine Homes.
watch: Siemens kept its Carmichael coal-mine rail contract in January 2020 despite protests. Woodbine racetrack gave an auction item; TD is not listed.
records_note: Names sponsors, donors and foundations on its funding page and lists its board, but links no annual reports or financial statements.

name: Oceania Centre for Arts, Culture and Pacific Studies (USP)
funding: A small unit of the University of the South Pacific (established 1997). Its 2026 residency is co-funded with Creative New Zealand and Creative Australia.
watch: Hosts the 2026 Oceania Pacific Arts Residency.
records_note: The centre has no records of its own; parent USP posts annual reports, audited statements for 2005 to 2025 and names its Council.

name: Official. Unofficial. Belarus (Belarus at the Venice Biennale, 2026 collateral event)
watch: 9 May–22 Nov 2026 at the church of San Giovanni Evangelista, San Polo 2454, an official collateral event of the 61st Biennale, curated by Daniella and Natalia Kaliada with Tsesler, Padhaiskaya, Hrynevich, Khalezin and chef Rasmus Munk; audio by Gillian Anderson, Stephen Fry, Jude Law and others. The state pavilion (Culture Ministry + NCCA, commissioner Kryshtapovich; last shown 2019, 'Exit') was absent in 2022 and 2024, so this is the first Belarusian presence since 2019 and it is unofficial.
records_note: A one-off Venice event run by Belarus Free Theatre, so the theatre's Companies House accounts and trustee list apply; no funder is named.

name: Ogden Museum
funding: Founder Roger Ogden's initial gift of about 600 works. The Helis Foundation funds free Thursday admission for Louisiana residents and presents the Poydras Corridor sculpture exhibition.
watch: The Helis family fortune came from oil. Its foundation currently pays for free Thursdays and the Poydras Corridor exhibition.
records_note: Names its trustees as of March 2026 but publishes no donor list, annual report or accounts; Form 990s for 2003 to 2025 sit on ProPublica.

name: Okayama Art Summit
funding: Okayama City, Okayama Prefecture and the Ishikawa Foundation lead the executive committee. Stripe International and Chugoku Bank are corporate partners. Foundation president Yasuharu Ishikawa directs the Summit.
watch: Citizens petitioned the city council and prefecture in 2021 and 2022 over harassment allegations against Ishikawa. Both were rejected; he directs the 2025 edition.
records_note: The 2025 summit site names its executive committee, sponsors and supporting agencies by name, but posts no reports or accounts.

name: Orange County Museum of Art
funding: Expenses $13.8M (2024); Segerstrom real-estate family and private donors; now UC Irvine Langson OCMA, a UC unit.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990s for 2012 to 2023 sit on ProPublica, the UC Irvine site names no donors, and no board is listed.
